name: The Philippian jailer
charge: Believing on the Lord with all his house the same night; washing the stripes of the men he had put in the stocks
summary: The keeper of the prison at Philippi, charged to keep Paul and Silas safely, thrust them into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks. At midnight they prayed and sang praises, and a great earthquake shook the foundations of the prison, and every door was opened and every band loosed. He drew his sword to kill himself, supposing the prisoners had fled, and Paul cried out that they were all there. He came trembling, asked what he must do to be saved, washed their stripes, and was baptized with all his house that same hour of the night.
offenseFull: The magistrates having commanded Paul and Silas to be beaten and cast into prison, the keeper of the prison received the charge to keep them safely, and having received that charge he thrust them into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks (Acts 16:23-24). The inner prison is the middle of the place, past the outer court, and it was pitch black in there. At midnight Paul and Silas prayed and sang praises to God, and the prisoners heard them; and suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened and every one’s bands were loosed (Acts 16:25-26). Get your mind on that level when you read it. They were not in there crying about how they could not get home. They were beaten and locked in the stocks and they prayed and sang, the same measure the Psalm sets, evening and morning and at noon, and the same three times a day Daniel kept with his windows open toward Jerusalem after the decree was signed (Psalms 55:17, Daniel 6:10). That is what the prayers of sincere men will do, and it is coming to us again, so our minds have to be conformed to it now.

The keeper of the prison, awaking out of his sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew out his sword and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had fled (Acts 16:27). The custom was that a guard who lost a prisoner on his watch was put to death in his place, and rather than face his superiors he decided in one moment to end himself. See how fast that level of sorrow moves in a man’s mind. His answer was not, I messed up, let me lead the manhunt and make it right; it was to take the one thing he had. The scripture says to love your own soul and comfort your heart, to put sorrow far away, because sorrow has killed many and there is no profit in it (Ecclesiasticus 30:23), and it says not to seek death in the error of your life nor pull destruction on yourself with the works of your hands, because God made not death and has no pleasure in the destruction of the living (Wisdom of Solomon 1:12-13). But Paul cried with a loud voice, telling him to do himself no harm, for they were all there (Acts 16:28). Why not let him do it? Because a man has to be given the chance to make it right. Understand what was about to be lost: a minute earlier he was ready to die, and salvation had not yet been offered to him.
judgmentFull: Then he called for a light, because it was black in there and he had to come down the hall by candle toward the voice he had heard, and he sprang in and came trembling and fell down before Paul and Silas, and brought them out and asked what he must do to be saved; and they told him to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and he would be saved, and his house, and they spoke the word of the Lord to him and to all that were in his house (Acts 16:29-32). That question is how we know what nation the man belonged to, because the one God exalted with his right hand to be a prince and a saviour was exalted to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins (Acts 5:31). He was an Israelite brother working as a guard, and he had just witnessed the power of God.

He took them the same hour of the night and washed their stripes, and was baptized, he and all his, straightway; and he brought them into his house and set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house (Acts 16:33-34). He escorted the men out of the jail to his own house, washed the wounds his own prison had put on them, fed them, and looked out for the prophets. The word was spoken to everyone in the house before the house was baptized, and the joy is recorded after the hearing and the believing.

In the morning the magistrates sent word to let the men go, and the keeper of the prison told Paul that he might depart in peace, but Paul required the magistrates to come themselves; and they came and besought them and brought them out and desired them to leave the city, and Paul and Silas went to the house of Lydia, saw the brethren and comforted them, and departed (Acts 16:35-40). The man charged with holding them fast had washed their wounds before the order to release them ever arrived.

text.text: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.
Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many, and there is no profit therein.
Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your hands.
For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living.
But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.
And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.
And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.

But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.
